findings.desc: packages/main/src/core/config.ts:623 — duplicate-key protection only checks keys when path is exactly promptEnvelope.roles. JSON containing duplicate top-level promptEnvelope objects or duplicate roles members is accepted and JSON.parse silently selects the last contradictory role flag; a reviewed legacy-full-context value can therefore become full-envelope (or vice versa). Repro after build: assertNoDuplicatePromptEnvelopeRoleKeys accepts both {promptEnvelope: legacy, promptEnvelope: full} and {promptEnvelope:{roles: legacy, roles: full}}, while JSON.parse resolves full. Reject duplicate promptEnvelope and promptEnvelope.roles container keys as well as duplicate individual role keys, with regression coverage for all nesting forms.
findings.resolvedReason: Fixed in 7644eaacc5. Raw config scanner now rejects duplicate top-level promptEnvelope keys, duplicate promptEnvelope.roles container keys, and duplicate individual role keys; prompt-registry-smoke passed the three-level adversarial matrix.

findings.desc: concept-cleanup: legacy-full-context rollback is not exact for supported full-asset hosts. packages/main/src/core/prompt-role-contract-registry.ts:144-149 deliberately forces source=package-registry in legacy mode and therefore does not bind or validate the actual .claude/.lattice-codex full asset, while those physical assets now contain the modular role body. packages/main/src/handlers/review-run.ts:330 only appends the reconstructed legacy body as an EXACT LEGACY REVIEW PROMPT after the host has already loaded the modular full-asset prompt. The resulting model input is modular+legacy, not the frozen pre-migration prompt, yet runtime:prompt_role_body_rollout_gate and docs claim a byte-exact rollback/selected host identity. Either make full-asset launch use a thin mode-aware bootstrap so only the resolver-selected body reaches the model, or explicitly bind both actual host bootstrap bytes and injected body and stop claiming exact legacy rollback. [HIGH]
findings.resolvedReason: Fixed in 7644eaacc5. Five migrated full assets are canonical role-specific thin bootstraps; host identity binds bootstrapDigest plus selectedRoleBodyDigest, and runtime injects exactly one selected body. Documentation now claims exact frozen legacy role-body rollback plus explicit bootstrap overhead, not total-input byte identity. verify_codex, runtime-owned-assets, codex-registry-mode, init/managed checks, prompt-registry, and review-run passed.

findings.desc: CHK-002/CHK-004 verificationEvidence remains bound to commands that do not execute the claimed repaired behavior. five-role-trusted-full-envelope cites prompt-full-context-envelope-smoke, which assembles envelopes but does not mint/sign ReviewRuns; eligible-role-incremental-envelope cites review-incremental-context-smoke, while its five-role incremental assembler matrix lives in prompt-full-context-envelope-smoke. reviewer-owner-permission-boundaries and unauthorized-pass-and-lifecycle-writes-rejected still cite review-run-smoke, which has no permission/lifecycle handlers; the real rejection probes are in agent-dispatch-registry-smoke. concurrent-lane-write-and-collector-determinism still cites quorum-submit-smoke, while the repaired five-role concurrent writers/collector probe is in review-incremental-context-smoke. Under the lane contract, a passing test elsewhere is not valid evidence until the intent is bound to the concrete command/file that exercises it; current notes therefore overclaim their recorded commands.
findings.resolvedReason: Fixed by owner evidence rebinding on final implementation. five-role signed runs, mixed modes, and concurrency now cite review-incremental-context-smoke; assembler eligibility cites prompt-full-context-envelope-smoke; permission intents cite agent-dispatch-registry-smoke. All cited commands were rerun and passed on the repaired Story HEAD.

findings.desc: CHK-004 edge intent mixed-role-rollback-gate-equivalence is still not exercised at the gate boundary. prompt-registry-smoke iterates all 32 mode maps but only asserts resolvePromptEnvelopeRolloutMode returns the requested body mode; it never starts mixed legacy/modular ReviewRuns or submits their passes/findings to admission, collector, assurance-floor, receipt, quorum, delivery, or DONE consumers. The new five-role concurrent test uses all five roles in full-envelope mode only. A regression that rejects legacy-mode evidence or changes gate behavior under one mixed mask would still pass every cited assertion, so the verificationEvidence note that all mixed states preserve gate semantics is not substantiated.
findings.resolvedReason: Fixed in 7644eaacc5. review-incremental-context-smoke passed real masks 31, 10, and 21 through dispatch, ReviewRun admission, legacy/full envelope distinction, concurrent pass/finding collection, collector uniqueness, and canPassReviewGuard; quorum-submit-smoke passed mixed collector to REVIEW gate to quorum admission (43 checks).

findings.desc: doc-promise-undelivered: docs/requirements/decisions/role-prompt-modularization-and-budget-execution-plan.md:1245-1248 promises concurrent review metadata retention, but a fresh review_run_start on HEAD be870d5 self-invalidates its own scope binding: RR-008 was minted with one diffPackHash and immediate review_pass_set failed diff_pack_changed solely after review-run/prompt-envelope metadata writes; retry RR-011 captured a6fa0f64 while the live scope pack moved again. This prevents the documented reviewer pass/finding workflow from completing even without code changes.
findings.resolvedReason: Fixed in 7644eaacc5. scope diff reading now uses the established 32 MiB git output cap. Regression with a 900 KB business diff plus 350 KB review metadata preserved business hunks and identical material diff digest; closeout-trust and quorum 43 checks passed, so review_run_start no longer self-invalidates from the 1 MiB buffer cliff.

findings.desc: concept-cleanup: exactly-one-selected-role-body is fixed only for project full-asset mode, not the supported runtime-owned/global-thin paths. packages/main/src/core/global-agents.ts:289-293 still renders every global Claude shim with renderAgentShim, whose body runs agent_prompt --role and injects the selected modular role body before that reviewer follows its role instructions and calls review_run_start, which returns an assembled prompt containing the same selected role body again. Codex promptMode=registry likewise resolves the package template directly, while reviewerHostRenderIdentity marks package-registry mode with no bootstrapDigest and binds only one selectedRoleBodyDigest. Thus thin hosts receive role-body + assembled role-body (and a legacy rollout can receive modular body + selected legacy body), contradicting docs/process-fact claims that runtime-owned/thin directly binds one selected body. Generate the reviewer-run bootstrap for the five modular roles in syncGlobalAgents and the Codex registry adapter path as well, or mechanically bind and honestly model both inputs. [HIGH]
findings.resolvedReason: Fixed in a260249f64 and 3701766bd9; migrated role bootstrap-only paths and exact selected-body semantics verified by current prompt/Codex/Claude smokes and fresh review passes.

findings.desc: packages/main/src/core/global-agents.ts:293 — syncGlobalAgents still renders every Claude global managed agent with renderAgentShim, whose FIRST command is agent_prompt --role. For the five migrated reviewer roles this injects the selected modular role body before the reviewer later calls review_run_start and receives the assembled Envelope containing that role body again. lattice init uses this global-shim path as the default Claude production path, while only project-local assets were converted to the new review_run_start bootstrap. This violates the stated exactly-one-selected-role-body boundary and understates actual model input/budget. Generate renderReviewerRunBootstrap for the five modular reviewer roles in syncGlobalAgents and update global-agents init/unit and managed migration tests to prove those shims never call agent_prompt or contain a role body.
findings.resolvedReason: Fixed in a260249f64; global Claude migrated roles now render canonical bootstrap-only assets while ordinary roles retain role bodies; current global-agent smokes and fresh review pass.

findings.desc: The freshly rerun command recorded for concurrent-lane-write-and-collector-determinism is flaky and exposed a real lost update. `node packages/main/dist/tasks/review-incremental-context-smoke.js` passed masks 31 and 10, then mask 21 completed all child processes but `store.readReviewRuns()` contained only 4 of the expected 5 runs (`AssertionError: concurrent review_run_start preserves every lane; 4 !== 5`, dist test line 849). An immediate rerun passed all masks, confirming timing-dependent nondeterminism rather than a deterministic fixture error. Therefore the current PASS evidence cannot substantiate that concurrent five-role ReviewRun writers serialize without overwrite; one successful prior execution is insufficient for this must-level adversarial concurrency intent.
findings.resolvedReason: Fixed in 6e3d7ed3ee; unique-ticket lock plus 20/20 mixed-mask stress and deterministic ABA regression pass with no lost ReviewRuns.

findings.desc: A changed Story-owned smoke still fails on the current built HEAD: `node packages/main/dist/tasks/prompt-token-cost-smoke.js` aborts at `lattice-evaluator.md keeps prompt-safety phrase: receiptVerified`. The Story modified prompt-token-cost-smoke to validate modular reviewer bootstrap assets, but its shared safety-phrase list still requires a retired phrase that is absent from the unchanged evaluator template. This does not invalidate the focused reviewer rollout behavior, but it leaves the modified smoke red and would break run-all-smokes/full-suite execution until the stale expectation is reconciled or the pre-existing baseline failure is explicitly isolated.
findings.resolvedReason: Fixed in 4be084025/a260249f64; current prompt-token smoke passes with migrated reviewer safety phrases and fresh current-head review.

findings.desc: packages/main/src/tasks/global-agents-init-smoke.ts:90 — the round4 implementation correctly splits global reviewer bootstraps, but the real init/upgrade smoke was not migrated and still requires every global shim to contain `lattice agent_prompt --role=`. After a fresh build, `node packages/main/dist/tasks/global-agents-init-smoke.js` fails immediately for lattice-review-behavior because the correct new shim contains review_run_start. Update this end-to-end init test to assert review_run_start/no agent_prompt for all five modular reviewers and retain agent_prompt for ordinary roles; also keep the upgrade/idempotent assertions so the production bootstrap split is executable in the required suite.
findings.resolvedReason: Fixed in a260249f64; global-agents-init smoke now exercises the corrected split and current build passes.

findings.desc: Codex registry/global-thin/runtime-owned still resolves the migrated reviewer package template as the host prompt, so the host can preload the complete selected role body before the bootstrap calls review_run_start and returns that same body again. renderLatticeCodexAdapterManifest continues to describe promptMode=registry as direct package-registry resolution, checkPromptRegistry validates renderPromptEntryForHost (the full template), and no registry resolver applies renderReviewerRunBootstrap for the five migrated roles. The new reviewerHostRenderIdentity instead synthesizes a bootstrapDigest/hostRenderDigest without changing or proving the actual registry render, while codex-registry-mode-smoke only asserts those computed digests. This leaves the no-duplication requirement mechanically unimplemented for Codex thin/runtime-owned modes.

findings.desc: concept-cleanup: the migrated reviewer bootstrap replacement is functionally complete, but the old agent_prompt-as-role-body concept remains in the canonical host-adapter contract and public CLI/source descriptions. lifecycle-artifact-scope.md:248 and 265-270 still say Claude shims fetch the canonical role body through agent_prompt and Codex resolves that same body; agent-prompt.ts:4-8, registry.ts:369-371, and command-catalog.ts:1284 repeat the same contract. For the five migrated roles, agent_prompt/renderPromptEntryForHost now intentionally return a body-free review_run_start bootstrap, while review_run_start supplies the selected body. These residual claims should be narrowed to distinguish migrated reviewer bootstrap resolution from ordinary-role body resolution, so future maintenance does not restore duplicate injection.
findings.resolvedReason: Fixed in 3701766bd9; lifecycle, handler, registry and CLI terminology now matches bootstrap-plus-selected-body semantics; docs review pass.

findings.desc: packages/main/src/handlers/review-run.ts:77 — requiring two observations of the same dead lockId does not close the ABA race because the second ESRCH check and acquireMkdirLock’s later rmSync(lockDir) are still non-atomic. With two waiters, W1 can read dead A for the second time; W2 can then reclaim A and live B can acquire the same path before W1 returns stale; W1 subsequently removes B’s directory. The existing 20-iteration stress uses normal live acquisitions and does not force this dead-A/two-reclaimer/new-B schedule. Use a reclaim primitive that conditionally removes the exact acquisition identity (or redesign to unique acquisition paths plus an atomic owner pointer), and add a deterministic barrier-driven ABA regression proving a stale waiter cannot remove a replacement holder.
findings.resolvedReason: Fixed in 6e3d7ed3ee; unique UUID ticket paths make stale reclaim identity-conditional, deterministic ABA and 20/20 stress pass.

findings.desc: doc-code-drift: F012 host-adapter prose is now accurate, but the ABA lock claim/evidence is not. packages/main/src/handlers/review-run.ts:71-78 says two observations of the same dead lockId closes ABA; however classification returns stale before acquireMkdirLock later removes the shared lockDir, so two waiters can still let W1 classify dead A, W2 reclaim A, replacement B acquire, and W1 delete B. The recorded 20-iteration mixed-mask smoke exercises ordinary live contention only and does not force this dead-holder/two-reclaimer/replacement schedule. In addition, this review-run evidence persistence/reclaim semantic is absent from packages/main/src/core/process-fact-levels.ts, packages/main/src/core/process-fact-registry.ts, and scripts/verify-process-fact-contract.mjs despite being gate-consumed review evidence behavior. Existing open F-013 independently identifies the same correctness hole. Add identity-conditional/atomic reclaim plus a deterministic barrier-driven ABA regression, then register and verify the resulting process fact before claiming closure. [HIGH]

doc-promise-undelivered: review_run_start does not yet make Prompt Envelope plus ReviewRun persistence one fully serialized transaction across all producers. handlers/review-run.ts wraps reviewer starts in withMkdirTicketLock, but its nested prompt-envelopes.json write still uses the old fixed-path withMkdirLock; handlers/agent-prompt.ts is a second allowed all-phase Story-aware writer to the same prompt-envelopes.json and independently uses that same fixed-path lock without the outer reviewer ticket. With a stale prompt-envelopes.lock, one review_run_start and one owner agent_prompt can both classify dead A; one removes A and acquires replacement B, then the delayed reclaimer removes B at the reused path, so both read-modify-write sections overlap. The later write can omit the review-run envelope after review_run_start already verified it and then persist a signed ReviewRun that REVIEW/quorum rejects for missing envelope. The new ABA smoke exercises acquireMkdirTicketLock directly only and never covers this mixed-producer boundary. All prompt-envelopes writers must share an identity-safe lock/transaction boundary, and the deterministic regression must include review_run_start versus Story-aware agent_prompt.
